task_2.title: Preserve user-modified compatibility plugins during 2.12.1 migration
task_2.description: Conan 2.12.1 fixes the compatibility plugin migration introduced in 2.12 so that the automatic merge of cppstd compatibility logic into compatibility.py only runs for Conan-generated files. If either compatibility plugin file has been user-modified, the migration is skipped to avoid overwriting custom behavior or deleting customized compatibility extensions.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Conan 2.12.1 does not overwrite or remove user-customized compatibility plugin files when applying the 2.12 compatibility migration.

expectation.grounded: During compatibility plugin migration, Conan should treat `compatibility.py` and `cppstd_compat.py` as migratable only when each file is missing or still marked as Conan-generated. The migration should update `compatibility.py` to the consolidated built-in compatibility implementation and remove `cppstd_compat.py` only when both files are safe to migrate. If either file appears user-modified, Conan should skip the migration and preserve existing files unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: When users upgrade, Conan should only perform the compatibility plugin migration on untouched default files. Any user-edited compatibility customization must be preserved, and the upgrade must not partially rewrite one compatibility file while leaving or deleting the other.

constraints.grounded: Do not overwrite an existing `compatibility.py` or delete an existing `cppstd_compat.py` when either file no longer identifies itself as Conan-generated. Preserve current behavior for fresh or untouched Conan-generated compatibility files, including consolidating cppstd compatibility into `compatibility.py` and eliminating the separate `cppstd_compat.py` file when migration is allowed.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must prevent loss of user customizations and avoid partial migrations, while still allowing automatic cleanup and consolidation for default, tool-managed compatibility files.

behavior: The default compatibility plugin content now contains the cppstd compatibility logic directly instead of loading it from a separate `cppstd_compat.py` module.
Compatibility migration evaluates both `compatibility.py` and `cppstd_compat.py` before applying changes.
A compatibility plugin file is considered safe to migrate only if it does not exist yet or still carries the Conan-generated marker at the start of the file.
If both compatibility plugin files are safe to migrate, Conan rewrites `compatibility.py` to the consolidated default content and removes `cppstd_compat.py` if it exists.
If either compatibility plugin file appears user-modified, Conan skips the migration entirely so existing compatibility files remain in place.
acceptance_criteria: When upgrading with untouched Conan-generated compatibility plugin files, Conan should end with a consolidated `compatibility.py` that includes cppstd compatibility behavior and should no longer keep a separate `cppstd_compat.py` file.
When `compatibility.py` has been user-edited before upgrade, the upgrade should leave that file unchanged and should not delete the existing `cppstd_compat.py` file as part of this migration.

When `cppstd_compat.py` has been user-edited before upgrade, the upgrade should leave that file unchanged and should not rewrite `compatibility.py` to the new consolidated default as part of this migration.
When one compatibility plugin file is safe to migrate but the other is user-modified, Conan should not perform a partial migration; both files should remain preserved as-is.

When a compatibility plugin file is absent and the remaining related file is still Conan-generated, Conan should be allowed to complete the migration and produce the consolidated default compatibility setup.

task_1.title: Restore full configuration reset behavior for conan config clean
task_1.description: Conan 2.12.1 fixes `conan config clean` so it fully resets the client configuration state. In 2.12.0, the clean operation could leave behind initialization state that prevented Conan from rebuilding all required default configuration files and directories, resulting in a partial reset instead of a true clean configuration.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan config clean` performs a complete configuration reset so Conan can regenerate every required default configuration artifact after the clean, while preserving the package storage area.

expectation.grounded: Running `conan config clean` should fully clear Conan's cleanable configuration state, including the state that indicates the default configuration structure is already initialized. After the clean, Conan should behave as needing default configuration regeneration and recreate the necessary default files and directories on subsequent normal initialization paths. The package storage location selected by `core.cache:storage_path` or its default equivalent must remain preserved.
expectation.conceptual: A configuration clean should act like a true reset of the user's Conan setup. After cleaning, Conan should rebuild any required default configuration structure instead of assuming it is still present, and the package cache itself should not be removed.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not delete the package storage directory or package contents. It should only correct the reset semantics of `conan config clean` so that stale initialization state does not block regeneration of required default configuration artifacts.
constraints.conceptual: The clean operation should reset configuration metadata without turning into a package cache wipe or changing unrelated Conan behavior.

behavior: `conan config clean` no longer leaves behind initialization state that can make Conan treat a partially cleaned home as already initialized.
After `conan config clean`, missing required default configuration files and directories are eligible to be regenerated by Conan's normal initialization flow.
The package storage area remains excluded from the clean operation.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan config clean`, Conan should fully reset its configuration state so later normal use can recreate the complete default configuration structure.

When the Conan home contains modified or missing default configuration artifacts before the clean, the clean should not leave Conan in a partially initialized state that prevents those artifacts from being recreated.
When `conan config clean` is executed, the package storage directory and its contents should remain intact.
